papers.title: GS I: History, Society, Geography
papers.about: Indian heritage and culture, modern history, world history, society, and world and Indian geography.

q.q: How did the Bhakti movement change the social and cultural life of medieval India?
q.dw: Discuss: look at several sides and reach a view.
pts: Intro: devotion over ritual; spread from the Tamil Alvars and Nayanars to the north
Challenged caste and priestly authority (Kabir, Ravidas, Chokhamela)
Growth of regional languages and literature (Tulsidas, Mirabai, Eknath)
New music and art forms; women saints
Bridge with Sufi ideas; limits: caste largely survived

q.q: Assess the role of the moderates in the early phase of the Indian national movement.
q.dw: Assess: weigh strengths and weaknesses, then judge.
pts: Who: Naoroji, Gokhale, Ranade, Pherozeshah Mehta (1885–1905)
Economic critique: drain theory, poverty and famines
Methods: petitions, prayers, protests; trained public opinion
Gains: Indian Councils Act 1892, a national platform
Limits: elite base, faith in British justice
Conclusion: laid the foundation that later phases built on

q.q: Why did the Revolt of 1857 fail? What were its long-term effects?
pts: Causes of failure: limited spread, no unified leadership or plan, princes and educated class stayed away
Effects: end of Company rule, Government of India Act 1858
Army reorganised; policy of non-interference with princes and religion
Divide and rule; seed of nationalism

q.q: Explain the factors that influence the distribution of rainfall during the Indian monsoon.
pts: Intro: monsoon as seasonal reversal of winds
Relief: Western Ghats and windward–leeward contrast; Shillong plateau and Mawsynram
Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea branches
Monsoon trough and depressions; ITCZ shift
Conclusion: variability and its effect on farming

q.q: Why are urban floods becoming more frequent in Indian cities? Suggest measures.
pts: Encroached lakes and floodplains, concrete surfaces
Old drainage, solid waste choking drains
Measures: sponge cities, restoring wetlands, early warning, zoning
Conclusion: urban planning with water at its centre

q.q: How does the joint family system in India adapt to urbanisation?
pts: Adaptation: functionally joint families, support across cities
Care of elders and children; women's double burden

q.q: Examine the role of women in India's freedom struggle.
pts: Early reformers and 1857 (Rani Lakshmibai, Begum Hazrat Mahal)
Gandhian phase: Sarojini Naidu, Kasturba, salt satyagraha marches
INA's Rani of Jhansi regiment (Lakshmi Sahgal)
Quit India: Aruna Asaf Ali, Usha Mehta's radio
Conclusion: freedom struggle also widened women's public role

q.q: Distinguish between the Nagara and Dravida styles of temple architecture.
pts: Nagara: north; curvilinear shikhara; no boundary walls usually; Khajuraho, Konark
Dravida: south; pyramidal vimana; gopurams; enclosure walls and tanks; Brihadeeswara
Vesara as a mixed style (Chalukya, Hoysala)

papers.title: GS II: Polity, Governance, Social Justice, IR
papers.about: Constitution, institutions, federalism, governance, welfare and international relations.

q.q: Discuss the role of the Governor in a federal setup in the light of recent disputes with state governments.
pts: Articles 153–167; dual role as agent of Centre and head of state
Disputes: delay on bills, summoning the House, appointment of chief ministers
Supreme Court rulings on assent to bills (2023–25)
Way forward: fixed timelines, consultation on appointment
Conclusion: Governor as a bridge, not a rival

q.q: How far has the anti-defection law achieved its purpose?
pts: Purpose: political stability, curb 'aaya ram gaya ram'
Gaps: merger clause, Speaker's delay and bias
Reforms: tribunal or ECI to decide, time limit

q.q: What is the significance of the 73rd Amendment? Why do panchayats remain weak?
pts: Constitutional status, three tiers, elections, reservation, State Finance Commission
Sarpanch-pati; capacity gaps; dependence on grants
Measures: own revenue, activity mapping, training

q.q: Evaluate the role of self-help groups in women's empowerment.
India's Neighbourhood First policy faces new challenges. Discuss.
pts: Challenges: China's presence, political changes in neighbours
Positive cases: power trade with Nepal and Bhutan, lines of credit
Way forward: quick delivery of projects, people-to-people links

q.q: Should India get a permanent seat in the UN Security Council? Give arguments.
pts: Obstacles: P5 veto, Uniting for Consensus

q.q: Examine the importance of the Right to Information Act for good governance and the concerns about its working.
pts: Concerns: pending appeals, vacancies in commissions, 2019 amendment
DPDP Act 2023 change to the personal-information exemption

q.q: How can technology make public service delivery more inclusive?
pts: Digital divide: women, elderly, rural areas
Assisted access through common service centres

papers.title: GS III: Economy, Environment, S&T, Security
papers.about: Economy and agriculture, infrastructure, science and technology, environment, disasters and internal security.

q.q: Why is India's manufacturing share of GDP stuck despite many schemes? Suggest measures.
pts: Hurdles: logistics cost, power, land, labour laws, MSME credit
Positive signs: electronics and mobile exports
Measures: skill, ease of doing business, R&D, FTAs

q.q: Discuss the need for crop diversification in Punjab and Haryana.
What are the challenges in India's energy transition? How can they be met?
pts: Targets: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030, net zero 2070
Coal dependence, grid storage, DISCOM finances

q.q: Explain the significance of the Digital Public Infrastructure model for India's economy.
pts: Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, ONDC, Account Aggregator

q.q: Discuss the causes of human–wildlife conflict in India and the measures to reduce it.
pts: Habitat loss, fragmented corridors, crop raiding
Elephants in Kerala and Odisha, leopards in Maharashtra
Measures: corridors, early warning, quick compensation

q.q: Mangroves are the first line of defence against coastal disasters. Explain.
pts: Reduce wave energy and storm surge

q.q: Left-wing extremism has shrunk. What should be done to keep it from returning?
pts: Trust building and good local governance

q.q: What are the uses and risks of artificial intelligence in governance?
pts: Uses: grievance redress, crop advice, health diagnostics, traffic

papers.title: GS IV: Ethics
papers.about: Ethics, integrity and aptitude: concepts, thinkers and case studies.

q.q: What do you understand by 'integrity'? Why is it important for a civil servant?
pts: Definition: consistency between values and actions
Honesty when no one is watching
Public trust and resistance to pressure

q.q: Distinguish between attitude and aptitude. Which matters more in public service?
pts: Attitude: way of thinking and feeling
Aptitude: ability to learn and do
Both needed; attitude guides the use of aptitude

q.q: Emotional intelligence helps an officer handle a crisis. Illustrate.
pts: Example: managing a mob or disaster relief

q.q: Case study: You are a district officer. A contractor close to a local leader is delaying a hospital building and offers you a 'gift' to overlook it. What will you do?
q.dw: Case study: options, then your choice with reasons.
pts: Stakeholders: patients, public, contractor, leader, you
Options: accept (unethical), ignore, act by the rules
Choose: refuse, document, issue notice, penalty clauses, inform superiors

q.q: 'The weak can never forgive. Forgiveness is the attribute of the strong.' What does this mean today?
pts: Use in public life and conflict resolution

q.q: What is meant by 'conflict of interest'? How should a civil servant deal with it?

papers.title: Essay
papers.about: Two essays of about 1,000–1,200 words each in the real paper. Plan for 15 minutes, write for 75.

q.q: A society that values its teachers values its future.
q.dw: Essay: plan with a mind map first.
pts: Present problems: vacancies, contract teachers, training

q.q: Technology is a good servant but a bad master.
pts: Balance through ethics, regulation and digital literacy

q.q: The forest is a gift we hold in trust for those not yet born.
